Implement the following plan:

# Slice 5.6 — musl port: fresh `musl-minixrs` fork at v1.2.6, and C on minix.rs

## Context

Phase 5's slice 5.6 is **milestone A**: a C program compiled against the musl
fork runs on minix.rs, exec'd out of the boot archive, with `printf` reaching
serial through VFS → TTY. Everything under it has shipped — grants (5.2), the
TTY console + CDEV band (5.3), the POSIX write path (5.4), and the SysV initial
stack that lets musl's crt run unpatched (5.5). Slice 5.6 is the first C in the
project and, per D8, the **ABI freeze point**.

Three corrections land with it:

1. **The fork is misnamed and cluttered.** It lives at
   `KevinBarnard/musl-minix` with a generic `CLAUDE.md` commit on its working
   branch and an untracked `linux-inventory.md`. Every plan already calls it
   **`musl-minixrs`** under the `minixrs` org. Start over: a **fresh fork**, no
   carried-over files.
2. **The base is stale.** The old fork sits at v1.2.5 + 103 commits. Upstream
   released **v1.2.6 on 2026-03-20**. The port starts from that tag.
3. **`minix` should be `minixrs` throughout.** `src/minixrs/`,
   `__minixrs_syscall`, and — since 5.6 is the ABI freeze and this is the last
   cheap moment — the generated C ABI surface too: `<minixrs/ipc.h>`,
   `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF`, `MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`.

## Decisions taken this session

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Fork creation | **Fresh** `minixrs/musl-minixrs` — a plain org repo (musl has no official GitHub repo), pushed from a clean clone of `git.musl-libc.org/git/musl`. **Archive** `KevinBarnard/musl-minix`; carry nothing over. |
| Branch layout | `main` = pristine upstream mirror, never committed to. `minixrs` = the port branch (default branch), based on tag `v1.2.6`, rebase-maintained onto future tags. |
| musl base | Tag **`v1.2.6`** — mirrors the tooling roadmap's tag-pinning convention (LLVM pins `llvmorg-22.1.8`). |
| Slice shape | Split **5.6a** (fork repo) / **5.6b** (minixrs), one slice number — the 4.6a/4.6b precedent, required by the cross-repo rule in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. |
| exec target | `PM_EXEC` gains a **16-byte name payload**; PM's hardcoded `EXEC_TARGET` goes away. init alternates `worker` / `hello`, so 5.5's exec-stack markers survive and hello's join them. Groundwork 5.9's path form needs anyway. |
| Naming sweep | Includes the generated headers and their macros (table in 5.6b §5). |

---

## Part 0 — create the fresh fork (do first)

1. **Archive** `KevinBarnard/musl-minix` on GitHub (Settings → Archive) so
   existing links resolve rather than 404. Nothing is carried out of it.
2. **Create** the empty repo `minixrs/musl-minixrs` under the org.
3. **Clone the canonical source and push**, in
   `$MINIXRS_FORKS_DIR/musl-minixrs` (default `~/src/minixrs-forks/…`; mount
   with `tooling/scripts/forks-volume.sh mount`):

   ```sh
   git clone https://git.musl-libc.org/git/musl musl-minixrs
   cd musl-minixrs
   git remote rename origin upstream
   git branch -m master main            # pristine mirror, upstream's content
   git remote add origin git@github.com:minixrs/musl-minixrs.git
   git push -u origin main --tags
   git checkout -b minixrs v1.2.6       # the port branch, pinned to the tag
   git push -u origin minixrs
   ```

   Then set `minixrs` as the repo's **default branch** so PRs target the port.

4. **Maintenance contract**, to be written into the fork's own doc:
   - `main` is never committed to. Refresh it with
     `git fetch upstream && git checkout main && git merge --ff-only upstream/master`.
   - The port branch is pinned to a **tag**, not to `main`'s head. Moving to a
     new release is deliberate:
     `git rebase --onto v1.2.7 v1.2.6 minixrs` then force-push.
   - Because the branch is force-pushed, the minixrs-side submodule pin is
     bumped in the same PR as any rebase.
5. **Fork docs**: one file on the `minixrs` branch only — `MINIXRS.md` — with
   the branch contract, the delta contract (below), and a re-derived Linux
   dependency inventory **against v1.2.6**. The old `CLAUDE.md` and
   `linux-inventory.md` are not carried over; the inventory is worth redoing,
   not copying, since it was written against v1.2.5.
6. Update the stale memory note `reference_local_repos.md` (it still records
   `~/src/learn/musl-minix`, musl v1.2.5, "one custom commit"), and the tooling
   repo's `docs/roadmap.md` fork-table row ("musl v1.2.5 fork" → v1.2.6, and
   the branch name).

---

## Slice 5.6a — the port (fork repo, its own session, branch `minixrs`)

**Delta contract** — the whole minixrs footprint, and nothing else:
`arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h`, `src/minixrs/`, `crt/crt1.c`'s brand block, and
`MINIXRS.md`. musl's `Makefile` globs `src/*/*.c`
(`SRC_DIRS = $(addprefix $(srcdir)/,src/* …)`), so **`src/minixrs/` is picked up
with no Makefile edit** — verified in the v1.2.6 tree.

**Gut the Linux syscall ABI**
- `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h`: `__syscall0..__syscall6` become calls to
  `__minixrs_syscall(n, a0..a5)`; delete `VDSO_USEFUL` / `VDSO_CGT_SYM` /
  `VDSO_CGT_VER`. Keep `__SYSCALL_LL_E/O` and `IPC_64`.
- `src/internal/syscall_ret.c` is untouched — minix.rs errnos are magnitudes
  `1..=40` and `>= 200` (D7), all inside the `> -4096UL` window.

**New `src/minixrs/`**
- `ipc.c` — the trap, byte-identical to `minix-ipc/src/lib.rs`: `x0` = endpoint,
  `x1` = primitive, `x2` = `&message`, `svc #0`, result back in `x0`.
- `_syscall.c` — `long __minixrs_syscall(long n, …)` dispatching on the Linux
  `__NR_*` numbers musl already emits:

  | Linux syscall | minix.rs mapping |
  |---|---|
  | `writev` | loop the iovecs, one `VFS_WRITE` each, sum the counts; report partial progress on a mid-loop error (POSIX) |
  | `write` | one `VFS_WRITE` |
  | `exit_group`, `exit` | `PM_EXIT` (does not return) |
  | `set_tid_address` | constant tid `1` |
  | `ioctl` | `-ENOTTY` — harmless, and it forces full buffering (see below) |
  | everything else | `-ENOSYS` (covers the link-satisfying set: `close`, `lseek`, `ppoll`, `openat`, `mmap`, `futex`, `read`) |

  Real `open`/`read`/`close` arrive in 5.8+.

**Brand `crt1.o`** — per `tooling/docs/abi-note.md`'s producer rules, the
28-byte `.note.minixrs.ident` block goes in `crt/crt1.c` as a `.pushsection`
global asm, so every C binary is branded regardless of driver. The kernel's
pack-time `scan_brand` assertion in `kernel/build.rs` then fails the *build* if
this regresses — it cannot silently rot.

**Runtime facts verified against the v1.2.6 source** — why the wrapper set is
this short. Re-confirm rather than assume:
- `__init_libc` returns early (`aux[AT_UID]==aux[AT_EUID] && … && !aux[AT_SECURE]`
  is all-zeroes-equal when the auxv omits them), so **`ppoll` never runs**.
- `__init_ssp(NULL)` falls back to `&__stack_chk_guard * 1103515245`; no syscall.
- `__init_tp` → `__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm on aarch64
  (v1.2.6 replaced the `.s` file); its only syscall is `set_tid_address`.
- `__init_tls(aux)` walks `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`/`AT_PHENT` — which 5.5 already
  supplies — and uses `builtin_tls` when there is no `PT_TLS`, so **no `mmap`**.
- `__stdout_write`'s `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)` failing sets `f->lbf = -1` → stdout is
  **fully buffered**, so `printf` output appears at `exit()`'s `__stdio_exit`
  flush. That makes the flush path part of the proof, not a detail.

---

## Slice 5.6b — the minixrs side

### 1. Vendoring (D9)

`.gitmodules` + submodule `external/musl` → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, tracking
the **`minixrs`** branch (not `main` — `main` has no port). First submodule in
the repo (`external/limine` is a Makefile fetch); `external/**` is already in
`sonar.exclusions`, and cargo-audit/deny/geiger only walk the cargo graph, so a
C tree is invisible to them.

### 2. `tools/build-musl.sh` (D10)

Drives configure/make into a cached sysroot at `target/musl-sysroot`:

- `cargo gen-c-headers target/gen-c-headers` first; pass
  `CFLAGS="-I<abs>/target/gen-c-headers/include"` so `src/minixrs/` sees
  `<minixrs/ipc.h>` under musl's `-nostdinc`.
- `CC="clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"`,
  `AR`/`RANLIB` = `$(rustc --print sysroot)/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-ar` /
  `llvm-ranlib` — **both already ship with the pinned toolchain**, so no
  Homebrew LLVM dependency. `--disable-shared`, `--prefix=target/musl-sysroot`.
- After `make install`, copy `target/gen-c-headers/include/minixrs/*.h` into
  `target/musl-sysroot/include/minixrs/` — never into the submodule working
  tree, which must stay pristine.
- **Make the D7 errno check real**: compile `abi-selftest.c` with
  `-DMINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO` against the fork's own `bits/errno.h` in
  the installed sysroot. Slice 5.0 explicitly deferred this to 5.6; until now
  CI proved macro spellings, not values.
- Write `target/musl-sysroot/.stamp` holding the submodule SHA + toolchain
  hash, for CI cache keying and build.rs's freshness check.

### 3. `userland/hello` — the first C program

Not a cargo crate; `hello.c` + `hello.ld` built directly by `kernel/build.rs`:

- Compile: `clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl -nostdinc
  -isystem target/musl-sysroot/include -ffreestanding -O2 -c`
- Link with **rust-lld** (`…/rustlib/*/bin/rust-lld -flavor gnu`), no platform
  linker: `crt1.o crti.o hello.o libc.a crtn.o`, plus D13's
  `-z max-page-size=4096 -z separate-loadable-segments`.
- `hello.ld` starts from `userland/worker/user.ld` verbatim — same 1 MiB base,
  same `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom (mandatory: without it lld's 64 KiB default page
  size leaves `e_phoff` unmapped and `AT_PHDR` points at nothing), same
  dual-assigned `.note.minixrs.ident` rule ahead of `/DISCARD/`. **It must also
  place what a musl link brings and a Rust one does not**: `.init`/`.fini`
  (crti/crtn), `.init_array`/`.fini_array` (walked by `__libc_start_init`),
  `.got`, `.data.rel.ro`. An orphan section placed past the last PT_LOAD is a
  silent load failure, so every input section gets an explicit home.
- Verify with `llvm-readobj --program-headers --elf-output-style=GNU` — a
  `user.ld` change is never assumed correct (CLAUDE.md rule).

`hello.c` prints three self-checking lines:
- `minix.rs hello: Hello from C!` — the milestone, via `printf` (buffered →
  flushed at `exit`, so it proves the flush path too).
- one `fprintf(stderr, …)` line — the unbuffered fd 2 path.
- `minix.rs hello: errno ok` — emitted only when `write(3, …)` returns `-1`
  **and** `errno == EBADF`. This is what makes the D7 errno identity observable
  at runtime rather than only at compile time, and it is self-checking in the
  5.3/5.4 `match=1` style.

### 4. Fallback when the sysroot is absent (D9, refined)

D9 says presence-check *the submodule*; check **the sysroot** instead
(`target/musl-sysroot/.stamp`), or a plain `cargo kernel-aarch64` on a fresh
clone silently triggers a multi-minute musl build. When the stamp is missing or
stale, `kernel/build.rs` emits a `cargo::warning` naming `tools/build-musl.sh`
and **packs the `worker` ELF under the name `hello`** — name-level fallback, so
boots stay green with no feature flag. Only the hello-specific markers vanish.

### 5. The `minix` → `minixrs` naming sweep

Fork-side names are 5.6a's. On this side the sweep is confined to
`tools/gen-c-headers` plus the two places that consume its output:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `include/minix/{ipc,com,callnr,errno}.h` | `include/minixrs/…` (`lib.rs:51-63`, `selftest.rs:14-17`) |
| `_MINIX_IPC_H`, `_MINIX_COM_H`, `_MINIX_CALLNR_H`, `_MINIX_ERRNO_H` | `_MINIXRS_*_H` |
| `_MINIX_OFFSETOF` | `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF` (`ipc_h.rs`) |
| `MINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`, `_MINIX_ABI_CHECK_ERRNO_H` | `MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`, `_MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_ERRNO_H` |

Consumers to update in the same commit: the CI `c-headers` job's
`-DMINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO` and `-I` paths, and CLAUDE.md's reproduce-the-
gate snippet.

**Leave alone**: prose that names MINIX 3 the reference OS — e.g.
`callnr_h.rs:169-170`'s "Deviation from MINIX 3: its `<minix/callnr.h>` holds
POSIX syscall numbers". Those correctly cite MINIX 3's headers, not ours. Same
for `MINIX_RQ`-style band comments describing MINIX 3 heritage.

### 6. `PM_EXEC` gains a name (the exec-target fix)

Slice 5.6's written scope says "init's exec target flips worker → hello", but
that predates 5.5 making `worker` the exec-stack probe; flipping would retire
`[ksys SYS_EXEC] … name=worker` and `init: exec stack ok`. Instead:

- `kernel-shared/src/callnr.rs`: `PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF = 0`, reusing the existing
  `EXEC_NAME_LEN = 16`, with the usual `const _` bounds guards beside the
  `VFS_*_OFF` block.
- `servers/pm/src/main.rs`: delete `EXEC_TARGET`; `handle_exec` reads the
  NUL-padded name from the payload and passes it to the existing
  `sys_exec(system, caller_e, name)`. Empty name → `EINVAL`. The kernel side
  (`kernel/src/system/do_exec.rs`) is **already name-driven** — no change.
- `userland/init/src/main.rs`: alternate `worker` / `hello` across fork cycles.
- `tools/gen-c-headers/src/callnr_h.rs`: emit the payload offsets it currently
  refuses to (`VFS_FD_OFF`/`VFS_LEN_OFF`/`VFS_BUF_OFF`, `CDEV_*_OFF`,
  `PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF`); drop the "not emitted yet" comment and the negative
  assertion at `callnr_h.rs:445-473` that pins their absence. This is exactly
  the deferral 5.0 wrote down for this slice — `src/minixrs/_syscall.c` is the
  C that needs them.

### 7. Exec stack size — likely blocker, verify early

`load_exec_image` maps **one 4 KiB stack page**
(`kernel/src/arch/aarch64/userland.rs:472-503`). musl's
`__libc_start_main` → `__init_libc` → `__init_tls` chain plus `vfprintf` (whose
frame carries the `nl_arg`/`nl_type` arrays) is plausibly over that budget.
Measure first; if it overflows, grow the exec stack to 4 pages mapped
**downward** from the existing top `SERVER_STACK_VA + PAGE_SIZE`, keeping the
top VA fixed so 5.5's `[exec] … sp=0x` marker and the
`USER_DEVICE_WINDOW_BASE` guard at `userland.rs:154` stay meaningful. Overflow
is not silent — it faults below the mapped page, VM finds no region, and the
SIGSEGV path fires.

### 8. CI

- `qemu-smoke` (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`): checkout with `submodules: recursive`; add
  a `tools/build-musl.sh` step **before** `cargo kernel-aarch64`; cache
  `target/musl-sysroot` keyed on the submodule SHA + `rust-toolchain.toml`.
  clang is already a hard build requirement (build.rs assembles the kernel's
  `.S` files with it) and `llvm-ar` ships with the pinned toolchain, so there
  is nothing new to install.
- `c-headers` keeps its hermetic syntax check (renamed macro/paths); the real
  errno **value** check now runs inside `build-musl.sh` on the smoke job,
  against the fork's actual `bits/errno.h`.
- `clippy-kernel` needs no submodule — it hits the worker-as-hello fallback.

### 9. Licensing + docs

- `external/musl/` gets a short README in the `external/limine/README.md`
  shape recording musl's **MIT** license and the pinned fork/branch;
  cargo-deny cannot see a C tree, so this is the only record.
- New `book/src/` chapter on the C toolchain and the musl port (the mdBook is
  canonical; `docs/*.md` is legacy).
- Marker bookkeeping in **both** places: flip 5.5 → `✓ shipped`, 5.6 →
  shipped, 5.7 → `◀ next`, in `docs/plan.md`'s Phase 5 table and
  `docs/plans/phase-5-musl-fs.md`. Record the *as built* deltas from the
  written scope — the a/b split, the `PM_EXEC` name form, sysroot-not-submodule
  presence check, the header rename — the way slice 5.0's "As built" block does.
- New CLAUDE.md bullet for slice 5.6 in the Code Conventions list.
- **Declare the ABI freeze (D8)**: after this slice, `Message` layout, call
  numbers, endpoints, and errnos change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR
  touching both repos.

---

## Verification

Boot markers added to `tests/qemu-boot.expected` (literal `grep -aF`
substrings, first-occurrence only — never counts, per the CI timing rule):

```
[ksys SYS_EXEC] target=15 name=hello entry=
minix.rs hello: Hello from C!
minix.rs hello: errno ok
```

`[ksys SYS_EXEC]` is head-carved at 6 and init alternates, so both the
`name=worker` and `name=hello` traces land inside the carve-out. The 5.5
markers (`[exec] argc=1 envc=0 auxv=4 sp=0x`, `minix.rs init: exec stack ok`)
must still pass — that is the point of alternating.

```sh
tools/build-musl.sh                       # sysroot + the real errno value check
cargo kernel-aarch64
timeout 25 cargo run -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --release > /tmp/boot.log 2>&1
tools/check-boot-log.sh /tmp/boot.log
timeout 25 cargo run … --no-default-features > /tmp/boot-nostubs.log   # stub-free config
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none -- -D warnings
cargo clippy -p minixrs-kernel --target aarch64-unknown-none --no-default-features -- -D warnings
cargo test -p minixrs-kernel-shared -p minixrs-gen-c-headers -p minixrs-pm
"$(rustc --print sysroot)"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-readobj --program-headers \
  --elf-output-style=GNU target/hello/hello        # hello.ld is a new linker script
```

Mutation tests (the 5.1–5.5 standard — apply, watch the named marker move,
revert from a scratchpad copy, never `git checkout`):

| Mutation | Expected |
|---|---|
| Drop the `crt1.c` brand block | kernel build **fails** at `pack_mxbi`'s `scan_brand` assertion — not a boot failure |
| `__minixrs_syscall`'s `writev` handles one iovec instead of looping | `Hello from C!` truncated or missing; `errno ok` survives |
| Return `0` instead of `-EBADF` from the `write(3,…)` path | `minix.rs hello: errno ok` vanishes, everything else stays |
| Point `PM_EXEC` back at a hardcoded `"worker"` | `name=hello` and both hello lines vanish; 5.5's markers survive — proves the alternation is live |
| Revert `hello.ld`'s `FILEHDR PHDRS` | `[exec] … auxv=1`, and musl's `__init_tls` walks an unmapped `AT_PHDR` |

Before recording any mutation result, confirm the build actually compiled
(`grep -a 'error\[E' <log>`, or check unrelated markers still PASS) — a build
failure and a successful mutation are indistinguishable in a boot log.

## Risks

- **4 KiB exec stack** — §7. Most likely thing to bite; measure before writing
  much else.
- **`configure` with `CC="clang --target=…"`** — D10's approach, unproven on
  this machine until 5.6b §2 runs. Fallback is the wrapper script musl also
  supports.
- **Force-pushed port branch vs. submodule pin** — a rebase orphans the pinned
  SHA; bump `external/musl` in the same PR as any fork rebase.
- **Sysroot build time in CI** — mitigated by the SHA-keyed cache; a cold cache
  costs one musl build on the arm64 runner.
- **Nothing may write into the tree.** The `c-headers` job asserts a clean
  `git status`; `build-musl.sh` keeps every artifact under `target/` and leaves
  `external/musl` pristine.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/kevinbarnard/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.2.0/skills/executing-plans

# Executing Plans

## Overview

Load plan, review critically, execute all tasks, report when complete.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the executing-plans skill to implement this plan."

**Note:** Tell your human partner that Superpowers works much better with access to subagents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Codex App, Copilot CLI, and Gemini CLI all qualify; see the per-platform tool refs in `../using-superpowers/references/`). If subagents are available, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development instead of this skill.

## The Process

### Step 1: Load and Review Plan
1. Ensure an isolated workspace: use superpowers:using-git-worktrees to create one or verify the existing one
2. Read plan file
3. Review critically - identify any questions or concerns about the plan
4. If concerns: Raise them with your human partner before starting
5. If no concerns: Create todos for the plan items and proceed

### Step 2: Execute Tasks

For each task:
1. Mark as in_progress
2. Follow each step exactly (plan has bite-sized steps)
3. Run verifications as specified
4. Mark as completed

### Step 3: Complete Development

After all tasks complete and verified:
- Announce: "I'm using the finishing-a-development-branch skill to complete this work."
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:finishing-a-development-branch
- Follow that skill to verify tests, present options, execute choice

## When to Stop and Ask for Help

**STOP executing immediately when:**
- Hit a blocker (missing dependency, test fails, instruction unclear)
- Plan has critical gaps preventing starting
- You don't understand an instruction
- Verification fails repeatedly

**Ask for clarification rather than guessing.**

## When to Revisit Earlier Steps

**Return to Review (Step 1) when:**
- Partner updates the plan based on your feedback
- Fundamental approach needs rethinking

**Don't force through blockers** - stop and ask.

## Remember
- Review plan critically first
- Follow plan steps exactly
- Don't skip verifications
- Reference skills when plan says to
- Stop when blocked, don't guess
- Never start implementation on main/master branch without explicit user consent

/* SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause */
/* Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors */
/*
 * GENERATED FILE -- DO NOT EDIT.
 *
 * IPC message format, endpoint packing, and the IPC primitive numbers.
 *
 * Produced by tools/gen-c-headers from the live constants in the
 * minixrs-kernel-shared crate:
 *     kernel-shared/src/message.rs
 *     kernel-shared/src/endpoint.rs
 *     kernel-shared/src/ipc_const.rs
 * Regenerate with `cargo gen-c-headers`.
 *
 * A build artifact, deliberately never committed (phase-5 decision D8):
 * the Rust constants are the single source of truth, so drift is
 * impossible by construction rather than caught by a test.
 */

#ifndef _MINIX_IPC_H
#define _MINIX_IPC_H

/*
 * This header deliberately includes nothing in the common case: it
 * describes a kernel ABI and must be usable from freestanding C as well as
 * from musl user space. The one thing it needs is offsetof, which comes
 * from a compiler builtin under a private name -- both to avoid depending
 * on <stddef.h> and to avoid ever colliding with the C library's own
 * offsetof macro.
 *
 * The fallback exists for a hypothetical non-GNU-flavoured compiler; the
 * supported toolchain is clang (phase-5 decision D10).
 */
#if defined(__GNUC__) || defined(__clang__)
#define _MINIX_OFFSETOF(t, m)    __builtin_offsetof(t, m)
#else
#include <stddef.h>   /* offsetof */
#define _MINIX_OFFSETOF(t, m)    offsetof(t, m)
#endif

/* ---- endpoints ---- */
typedef int endpoint_t;
_Static_assert(sizeof(int) == 4, "the minix.rs ABI assumes a 32-bit int for endpoint_t");

#define ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT       15
#define ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK       0x7fff
#define ENDPOINT_MAX_GENERATION  65535
#define ENDPOINT_SLOT_TOP        16383

#define ANY                      ((endpoint_t) 16383)
#define NONE                     ((endpoint_t) 16382)
#define SELF                     ((endpoint_t) 16381)

/*
 * Endpoint packing. minix.rs deviates from MINIX 3 deliberately: the proc
 * field is SIGN-EXTENDED from bit ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT-1 to recover negative
 * kernel-task slots, rather than MINIX 3's MAX_NR_TASKS offset bias. These
 * mirror endpoint.rs::{make_endpoint, endpoint_proc, endpoint_gen}.
 *
 * The consequence is that _ENDPOINT(0, p) != p for negative p, which is why
 * minix/com.h gives every process both a _PROC_NR and an _EP macro.
 */
#define _ENDPOINT(g, p)  (((g) << ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT) | ((p) & ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK))
#define _ENDPOINT_G(e)   ((e) >> ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT)
#define _ENDPOINT_P(e)                                                   \
    ((((e) & ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK) & (1 << (ENDPOINT_GEN_SHIFT - 1)))      \
        ? (((e) & ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK) | ~ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK)             \
        : ((e) & ENDPOINT_PROC_MASK))

/* ---- message ---- */

/*
 * The IPC message. Laid out to match kernel-shared's #[repr(C, align(8))]
 * Message exactly; the assertions below are generated from the live Rust
 * type, so a layout change on either side fails to compile rather than
 * silently corrupting every IPC call.
 *
 * C11 forbids an alignment specifier on a struct type declaration, so the
 * _Alignas rides the first member -- a struct's alignment is the maximum of
 * its members', which yields the required 8.
 */
struct message {
    _Alignas(8) endpoint_t m_source;   /* set by the kernel on delivery */
    int                    m_type;     /* call number out, result back  */
    unsigned char          payload[96];
};
typedef struct message message;

_Static_assert(sizeof(message) == 104, "message size drifted from kernel-shared Message");
_Static_assert(_Alignof(message) == 8, "message alignment drifted from kernel-shared Message");
_Static_assert(_MINIX_OFFSETOF(message, m_source) == 0, "m_source offset drifted from kernel-shared Message");
_Static_assert(_MINIX_OFFSETOF(message, m_type) == 4, "m_type offset drifted from kernel-shared Message");
_Static_assert(_MINIX_OFFSETOF(message, payload) == 8, "payload offset drifted from kernel-shared Message");

/* ---- IPC primitives ---- */

/*
 * Primitive numbers for the IPC trap. The register that carries them is
 * part of the per-architecture trap ABI -- see kernel-shared/src/ipc_const.rs
 * and the minix-ipc crate, which are authoritative.
 */
#define SEND                     1
#define RECEIVE                  2
#define SENDREC                  3
#define NOTIFY                   4
#define SENDNB                   5
#define SENDA                    16
#define MINIX_KERNINFO           32
#define NOTIFY_MESSAGE           0x1000

#endif /* _MINIX_IPC_H */

# The minixrs ELF identity note (normative)

Every minixrs user-space executable carries a NetBSD-style ELF note that
identifies it as a minixrs binary and states which minixrs ABI it was built
for. The kernel (and any other consumer — mkfs, pack-time assertions,
`verify/check-brand.sh`) verifies this note before running the binary.

`EI_OSABI` in the ELF header stays `0` (`ELFOSABI_NONE`) **permanently**. The
note is the sole identity mechanism. This is deliberate: stock binutils, gdb,
lldb, and every other ELF consumer keep working with no patches, forever.

## Note format

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Section name | `.note.minixrs.ident` |
| Section type | `SHT_NOTE`, flags `SHF_ALLOC` |
| Alignment | 4 bytes |
| Owner (name) | `"minixrs\0"` — `namesz = 8` |
| Type | `NT_MINIXRS_IDENT = 1` |
| Descriptor | 2 × u32 little-endian: `[abi_version, flags]` — `descsz = 8` |
| `abi_version` | currently `1` |
| `flags` | `0`, all bits reserved (must be written as 0) |

Program-header placement: the note gets a **dedicated `PT_NOTE`** program
header (`p_flags = PF_R`), and the section is also placed at the **start of
the read-only `PT_LOAD`** segment. Consumers locate the note by walking
`PT_NOTE` program headers, never by section name — sections may be stripped.

## Exact byte layout (28 bytes)

```
offset  bytes                    field
0x00    08 00 00 00              namesz = 8
0x04    08 00 00 00              descsz = 8
0x08    01 00 00 00              type   = NT_MINIXRS_IDENT (1)
0x0c    6d 69 6e 69 78 72 73 00  name   = "minixrs\0"
0x14    01 00 00 00              desc[0] = abi_version = 1
0x18    00 00 00 00              desc[1] = flags = 0
```

Both name and descriptor are already 4-byte multiples, so no padding is
emitted.

## Consumer rules

1. Walk `PT_NOTE` program headers only. Iterate the note records inside each
   segment (`namesz`/`descsz` are padded up to 4-byte multiples between
   records).
2. **Ignore** notes whose owner is not exactly `"minixrs\0"` or whose type is
   not `NT_MINIXRS_IDENT` (foreign-owner notes are normal and harmless).
3. Accept `descsz >= 8`. Read **only** the words you know
   (`abi_version`, `flags`); never reject a note for being longer than
   expected — that is how the format grows.
4. **Reject** an unknown `abi_version` (`!= 1` today) — the binary was built
   for an ABI this consumer does not speak.
5. A binary with no matching note is **not a minixrs binary**; the kernel
   refuses to execute it (`ElfError::MissingBrand` /
   `ElfError::UnsupportedAbi` in minixrs).

/*
 * The minixrs ELF identity note (tooling/docs/abi-note.md, normative).
 *
 * The kernel REFUSES to load an unbranded ELF, so every C binary needs this
 * 28-byte note. It lives in crt1.c because crt1.o is linked explicitly into
 * every executable rather than pulled from an archive -- so it cannot be
 * dropped by archive-member selection the way a libc.a member could, and no
 * C program has to remember to opt in.
 *
 * Byte-for-byte the same record the Rust `minixrs_abi_note::brand!()` macro
 * emits, so a C binary and a Rust one are indistinguishable to the verifier:
 *
 *   namesz = 8, descsz = 8, type = NT_MINIXRS_IDENT (1),
 *   name = "minixrs\0", desc = [abi_version = 1, flags = 0]
 *
 * Both name and descriptor are already 4-byte multiples, so no padding is
 * emitted. The linker script must KEEP() this section and give it a dedicated
 * PT_NOTE at the start of the read-only PT_LOAD.
 *
 * Regressing this fails the minix.rs KERNEL BUILD, not the boot: kernel/build.rs
 * runs the same scan_brand check when it packs the boot archive.
 */
__asm__(
	".pushsection .note.minixrs.ident, \"a\", %note\n"
	".p2align 2\n"
	".long 8\n"
	".long 8\n"
	".long 1\n"
	".asciz \"minixrs\"\n"
	".long 1\n"
	".long 0\n"
	".popsection\n"

input.content:
# musl-minixrs — the minix.rs libc fork

This is [musl libc](https://musl.libc.org/) with its Linux syscall ABI replaced
by [minix.rs](https://github.com/minixrs/minixrs) IPC. It exists so that
ordinary C programs — compiled with an unmodified clang, linked against an
almost-unmodified musl — run on a MINIX-style microkernel where every OS
service is a user-space server reached by message passing.

musl is MIT licensed; see `COPYRIGHT`. This fork adds nothing under a different
licence.

## Branch layout

| Branch | What it is |
|---|---|
| `main` | A **pristine mirror** of upstream `master`. Never commit to it. |
| `minixrs` | The port. Based on tag **`v1.2.6`** (2026-03-20). The default branch. |

`main` exists so the fork is diffable against upstream without a second remote.
Refresh it with:

```sh
git fetch upstream
git checkout main
git merge --ff-only upstream/master
```

The port branch is pinned to a **tag**, never to `main`'s head — a libc that
moves under you is not a base you can debug a kernel against. Moving to a new
release is a deliberate act:

```sh
git rebase --onto v1.2.7 v1.2.6 minixrs
git push --force-with-lease origin minixrs
```

Because the port branch is force-pushed, **the minix.rs submodule pin must be
bumped in the same PR as any rebase** (`external/musl` in the minixrs repo). A
rebase orphans the previously pinned SHA, and a submodule pointing at an
orphaned commit fails to clone rather than failing loudly at build time.

## Delta contract

The port is deliberately tiny, and staying tiny is a design goal rather than an
accident — every file that stays byte-identical to upstream is a file that
rebases for free onto the next release. **The entire minix.rs footprint is:**

| Path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` | `__syscall0..6` call `__minixrs_syscall`; VDSO macros deleted |
| `src/minixrs/ipc.c` | The `svc #0` IPC trap |
| `src/minixrs/_syscall.c` | Linux syscall number → server IPC |
| `src/minixrs/minixrs_internal.h` | Shared declarations for the two above |
| `crt/crt1.c` | The 28-byte `.note.minixrs.ident` ELF brand |
| `MINIXRS.md` | This file |

Nothing else. `git diff v1.2.6 --stat` should show exactly two modified files
outside `src/minixrs/`.

**No Makefile change is needed** to build `src/minixrs/`: musl globs its source
directories (`SRC_DIRS = $(addprefix $(srcdir)/,src/* …)` in the `Makefile`), so
a new `src/<name>/` directory is picked up automatically. Verified against the
v1.2.6 tree.

`src/internal/syscall_ret.c` is **untouched on purpose**. It treats a return
value in `[-4095, -1]` as an errno, and minix.rs errno magnitudes are `1..=40`
and `>= 200` (phase-5 decision D7), so all of them land inside that window. The
POSIX block additionally uses the same values Linux and musl do, which is why
musl's stock `bits/errno.h` needs no edit either.

## The seam

musl's ~297 `__syscall` call sites are all unmodified. They still emit Linux
syscall numbers. `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` is the one place that knows
better: instead of executing `svc` with the number in `x8`, every `__syscallN`
calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the Linux number and issues the
corresponding server round-trip.

Keeping that shape — rather than rewriting call sites — is what lets the other
~1900 source files stay identical to upstream.

The IPC trap ABI is fixed by the kernel's `trap.S` and reproduced exactly in
`src/minixrs/ipc.c`. It is the C twin of the Rust `minix-ipc` crate:

```
x0 = endpoint (also receives the result)
x1 = IPC primitive (SEND / RECEIVE / SENDREC / NOTIFY / SENDNB)
x2 = pointer to the 104-byte message
svc #0
```

### Implemented syscalls

| Linux syscall | minix.rs mapping |
|---|---|
| `writev` | one `VFS_WRITE` per iovec, counts summed; partial progress reported on a mid-loop error |
| `write` | one `VFS_WRITE` |
| `exit_group`, `exit` | `PM_EXIT` (does not return) |
| `set_tid_address` | constant tid `1` |
| `ioctl` | `-ENOTTY` |
| everything else | `-ENOSYS` |

`ioctl` returning `-ENOTTY` is load-bearing rather than merely harmless:
`__stdout_write` sets `f->lbf = -1` when `TIOCGWINSZ` fails, which makes stdout
**fully buffered**. `printf` output is then flushed by `exit()`'s
`__stdio_exit`, so the flush path is exercised by any program that prints.

`writev` is the one that carries stdio — `__stdio_write` always calls `writev`,
never `write`, and loops until the returned count equals what it asked for. The
count returned must therefore be exact; over-reporting makes musl believe a
flush completed that did not.

## Linux dependency inventory (re-derived against v1.2.6)

musl references **341 distinct `SYS_*` numbers** across 297 call sites. The port
implements six. That is viable only because of what the startup path does *not*
do — each of the following was re-read in the v1.2.6 source, not assumed:

| Fact | Consequence |
|---|---|
| `__init_libc` returns early when `AT_UID==AT_EUID && AT_GID==AT_EGID && !AT_SECURE` — all read `0` when absent from the auxv | the secure-mode branch, the **only** `ppoll`/`open` in startup, never runs |
| `__init_ssp(NULL)` (no `AT_RANDOM`) derives the canary as `&__stack_chk_guard * 1103515245` | no syscall |
| `__init_tp` issues exactly one syscall, `set_tid_address` | `__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm on aarch64 (v1.2.6 replaced the `.s` file) |
| `__init_tls` uses the static `builtin_tls` when the program has no `PT_TLS` | no `mmap` |
| `__init_tls` walks `AT_PHDR` / `AT_PHNUM` / `AT_PHENT` | the kernel must supply them — minix.rs does, since slice 5.5 |
| `__set_thread_area` walks `libc.auxv` to mask SME hwcap bits | the auxv **must** be `AT_NULL`-terminated |

Tiers of what remains, roughly by distance:

- **Next up (minix.rs slice 5.8+):** `openat`, `read`, `close`, `lseek` — real
  file I/O, once there is a filesystem server. These are already referenced by
  code that links today; they simply answer `-ENOSYS`.
- **Needs kernel work:** `mmap`/`munmap`/`brk` (minix.rs has `VM_MMAP`/`VM_BRK`
  but no libc wiring), `futex` (no threads yet), signal delivery
  (`rt_sigaction` and friends — minix.rs signals default-terminate).
- **Wholly Linux, unlikely to ever be ported:** everything under `src/linux/`
  (`epoll`, `inotify`, `sendfile`, `prctl`, cgroup and namespace calls), plus
  `src/aio`, `src/mq`, and the netlink paths in `src/network`. These compile
  into `libc.a` and answer `-ENOSYS` if called; nothing links them in by
  accident.

## The ELF brand

Every minix.rs user-space binary carries a 28-byte `.note.minixrs.ident` note
(the normative spec is `docs/abi-note.md` in the minixrs tooling repo). The
kernel **refuses to load an unbranded ELF**.

The note is emitted from `crt/crt1.c` as a `.pushsection` global asm, so every C
binary gets it regardless of how it was linked, and no program has to opt in.
`crt1.o` is linked explicitly into every executable rather than pulled from an
archive, so — unlike a `libc.a` member — it can never be dropped by
archive-member selection.

Its bytes are identical to what the Rust `minixrs_abi_note::brand!()` macro
emits, so a C binary and a Rust one are indistinguishable to the verifier:

```
08 00 00 00              namesz = 8
08 00 00 00              descsz = 8
01 00 00 00              type   = NT_MINIXRS_IDENT
6d 69 6e 69 78 72 73 00  "minixrs\0"
01 00 00 00              abi_version = 1
00 00 00 00              flags = 0
```

A linker script consuming this libc must `KEEP()` the section and give it a
dedicated `PT_NOTE` at the start of the read-only `PT_LOAD`. Regressing the
brand fails the **minix.rs kernel build**, not the boot: `kernel/build.rs` runs
the same `scan_brand` check when it packs the boot archive.

## Building

The canonical build is `tools/build-musl.sh` in the minixrs repo, which drives
configure/make into a cached sysroot at `target/musl-sysroot`. To build by hand:

```sh
mkdir build && cd build
SR="$(rustc --print sysroot)"; AR=$(echo "$SR"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-ar)
../configure --target=aarch64-linux-musl --disable-shared \
  --prefix=/path/to/sysroot \
  CC="clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl" \
  AR="$AR" RANLIB="$AR s" \
  CFLAGS="-I/path/to/minixrs/target/gen-c-headers/include"
make && make install
```

Notes:

- Build **out of tree**. The minixrs repo vendors this as a submodule and its
  CI asserts a clean `git status`, so nothing may be written into the work tree.
- `RANLIB="$AR s"` rather than `llvm-ranlib`: the pinned Rust toolchain ships
  `llvm-ar` but **not** `llvm-ranlib`. `llvm-ar s` writes the archive index,
  which is all `ranlib` is for here.
- The `CFLAGS` `-I` is how `src/minixrs/*.c` finds `<minixrs/ipc.h>` under
  musl's `-nostdinc`. Those headers are generated by `cargo gen-c-headers` in
  the minixrs repo from the live Rust constants — they are a build artifact and
  are never committed to either repo.
- configure's linker probes all fail under Apple clang (its default linker is
  ld64). That is harmless: `--disable-shared` means only `libc.a` and the crt
  objects are produced, and consumers link with `rust-lld`.

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: BSD-3-Clause
# Copyright (c) 2025-2026 Kevin Barnard and minix.rs Contributors
#
# Build the musl fork (external/musl) into a cached sysroot at
# target/musl-sysroot (phase-5 decision D10).
#
# Everything this writes lives under target/. The submodule work tree is left
# PRISTINE -- the c-headers CI job asserts a clean `git status`, and a build
# that dirties a submodule would fail it. musl supports out-of-tree builds, so
# the object tree goes to target/musl-build.
#
# Rebuilds are skipped when target/musl-sysroot/.stamp already matches the
# submodule SHA and the toolchain. Pass --force to rebuild anyway.
#
# Environment:
#   MUSL_SRC   musl source tree (default: external/musl). Point this at a local
#              fork checkout to test a port change before bumping the submodule.

set -eu

ROOT=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
MUSL_SRC=${MUSL_SRC:-$ROOT/external/musl}
SYSROOT=$ROOT/target/musl-sysroot
BUILD=$ROOT/target/musl-build
HDRS=$ROOT/target/gen-c-headers
STAMP=$SYSROOT/.stamp

FORCE=0
[ "${1:-}" = "--force" ] && FORCE=1

if [ ! -f "$MUSL_SRC/configure" ]; then
	echo "error: no musl source at $MUSL_SRC" >&2
	echo "       run: git submodule update --init --recursive" >&2
	exit 1
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Toolchain. Both binutils replacements ship with the pinned Rust nightly, so
# there is no Homebrew LLVM dependency.
#
# RANLIB is `llvm-ar s`, not llvm-ranlib: the toolchain ships llvm-ar but NOT
# llvm-ranlib, and `llvm-ar s` writes the archive index, which is all ranlib
# does here.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
SR=$(rustc --print sysroot)
AR=$(echo "$SR"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-ar)
if [ ! -x "$AR" ]; then
	echo "error: llvm-ar not found under $SR/lib/rustlib/*/bin" >&2
	exit 1
fi
CC="clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Freshness. The stamp keys on the exact musl commit plus the toolchain, so a
# submodule bump or a nightly bump both invalidate it. CI uses the same value
# as its cache key.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
MUSL_SHA=$(git -C "$MUSL_SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
TOOLCHAIN_ID=$(
	{ cat "$ROOT/rust-toolchain.toml" 2>/dev/null || true; clang --version | head -1; } \
		| shasum | cut -d' ' -f1
)
WANT="musl=$MUSL_SHA toolchain=$TOOLCHAIN_ID"

if [ "$FORCE" -eq 0 ] && [ -f "$STAMP" ] && [ -f "$SYSROOT/lib/libc.a" ]; then
	if [ "$(cat "$STAMP")" = "$WANT" ]; then
		echo "musl sysroot up to date ($SYSROOT)"
		exit 0
	fi
fi

echo "building musl fork -> $SYSROOT"
echo "  source:    $MUSL_SRC ($MUSL_SHA)"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The generated ABI headers come first: src/minixrs/*.c includes <minixrs/ipc.h>
# and friends, and musl compiles its own sources with -nostdinc, so the only way
# in is an explicit -I in CFLAGS.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
( cd "$ROOT" && cargo gen-c-headers >/dev/null )

rm -rf "$BUILD" "$SYSROOT"
mkdir -p "$BUILD"

( cd "$BUILD" && "$MUSL_SRC/configure" \
	--target=aarch64-linux-musl \
	--prefix="$SYSROOT" \
	--disable-shared \
	CC="$CC" \
	AR="$AR" \
	RANLIB="$AR s" \
	CFLAGS="-I$HDRS/include" >/dev/null )

# configure's linker probes all fail under a Darwin-hosted clang (its default
# linker is ld64). Harmless: --disable-shared means only libc.a and the crt
# objects are built, and consumers link with rust-lld.

make -C "$BUILD" -j"$(getconf _NPROCESSORS_ONLN 2>/dev/null || echo 4)" >/dev/null
make -C "$BUILD" install >/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Install the generated minix.rs ABI headers alongside musl's own, so a C
# program compiles against one -isystem path. They are copied into the SYSROOT,
# never into the submodule work tree.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
mkdir -p "$SYSROOT/include/minixrs"
cp "$HDRS"/include/minixrs/*.h "$SYSROOT/include/minixrs/"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The D7 errno check, for real.
#
# Slice 5.0 deferred this to 5.6 because CI had no musl sysroot: until now the
# opt-in POSIX block was only ever compiled against a generated stand-in, which
# proves macro spellings but not values. Here it compiles against the FORK'S OWN
# bits/errno.h in the installed sysroot, so a POSIX errno whose value drifted
# from musl's is a build failure.
#
# -nostdinc + -isystem "$SYSROOT/include" is what makes it honest: the host libc
# cannot creep in (Darwin EDEADLK is 11, not 35).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
echo "  checking:  POSIX errno values against the fork's bits/errno.h"
clang -std=c11 -pedantic-errors -Wall -Wextra -Werror -fsyntax-only \
	--target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl \
	-nostdinc -isystem "$SYSROOT/include" \
	-DMINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO \
	"$HDRS/abi-selftest.c"

printf '%s' "$WANT" > "$STAMP"
echo "musl sysroot ready ($SYSROOT)"

input.content:
# external/ — vendored third-party code

Two different vendoring mechanisms live here, for two different reasons.

| Directory | Mechanism | Upstream | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limine/` | `make` fetch of a pinned commit (artifacts gitignored) | [limine-bootloader/limine](https://github.com/limine-bootloader/limine) | BSD Zero Clause |
| `musl/` | git submodule, pinned commit on branch `minixrs` | [minixrs/musl-minixrs](https://github.com/minixrs/musl-minixrs) | MIT |

See `limine/README.md` for the bootloader. The rest of this file covers musl.

## `musl/` — the libc fork (slice 5.6)

`external/musl` is a submodule of **`minixrs/musl-minixrs`**, our fork of
[musl libc](https://musl.libc.org/), tracking its **`minixrs`** branch — *not*
`main`, which is a pristine upstream mirror with no port on it. The fork is
based on upstream tag `v1.2.6`.

musl is **MIT licensed**; the fork adds nothing under a different licence. This
table is the only record of that fact in this repo: `cargo-deny` and
`cargo-audit` walk the cargo dependency graph, which a C source tree is invisible
to, so nothing automated can notice the licence here.

Initialise it with:

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

### Building it

`tools/build-musl.sh` drives configure/make into a cached sysroot at
`target/musl-sysroot`. Everything it writes lives under `target/`; the submodule
work tree is left **pristine**, because the `c-headers` CI job asserts a clean
`git status` and a build that dirtied a submodule would fail it.

Nothing builds musl automatically. `kernel/build.rs` presence-checks
`target/musl-sysroot/.stamp` and, when it is missing or stale, packs the
`worker` ELF under the name `hello` and emits a `cargo::warning` — so a fresh
clone still boots green, it just loses the slice-5.6 C markers. Kicking off a
multi-minute libc build from inside a cargo build script would be worse.

### Bumping the pin

The port branch is **force-pushed** when it is rebased onto a new upstream tag,
which orphans whatever commit this submodule pins. So a fork rebase and the
submodule bump here must land in the **same PR** — otherwise this repo points at
a commit that no longer exists and the submodule fails to clone.

The fork's own `MINIXRS.md` carries the branch contract, the delta contract, and
a Linux-dependency inventory re-derived against v1.2.6.

input.content:
# The C toolchain and the musl port

Slice 5.6 is Phase 5's **milestone A**: an ordinary C program, compiled against
a forked musl and linked with `rust-lld`, running on minix.rs with `printf`
reaching the serial console.

Nothing in that program is minix.rs-specific — it is plain C against plain
`<stdio.h>`. It works because the libc underneath it was ported, not because the
program was. That is the whole point of the exercise.

```c
printf("minix.rs hello: Hello from C!\n");
```

```
minix.rs hello: Hello from C!
```

## Where the pieces live

| Piece | Location |
|---|---|
| The libc fork | `external/musl` (submodule → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, branch `minixrs`) |
| Sysroot builder | `tools/build-musl.sh` → `target/musl-sysroot` |
| The C program | `userland/hello/{hello.c,hello.ld}` |
| Compile + link | `kernel/build.rs`'s `build_hello` |
| Generated ABI headers | `cargo gen-c-headers` → `target/gen-c-headers/include/minixrs/` |

## The seam: Linux syscall numbers in, IPC out

minix.rs has no Linux syscall ABI. Its only `svc #0` entry point is the MINIX
IPC trap, and every OS service is a user-space server reached by message
passing. Yet musl is written throughout in terms of `__syscall(SYS_write, …)`.

The port resolves this in **one file**. `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` normally
executes `svc` with the syscall number in `x8`; in the fork, every `__syscallN`
instead calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the Linux number and issues
the corresponding server round-trip:

| Linux syscall | minix.rs mapping |
|---|---|
| `writev` | one `VFS_WRITE` per iovec, counts summed |
| `write` | one `VFS_WRITE` |
| `exit_group`, `exit` | `PM_EXIT` (does not return) |
| `set_tid_address` | constant tid `1` |
| `ioctl` | `-ENOTTY` |
| everything else | `-ENOSYS` |

Keeping musl's ~297 call sites unmodified is what lets the other ~1900 source
files stay byte-identical to upstream — and therefore rebase for free onto the
next release. The **entire** fork delta is `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h`,
`src/minixrs/`, a brand block in `crt/crt1.c`, and a `MINIXRS.md`.

Six syscalls is enough only because musl's startup path avoids the rest: with
`AT_UID`/`AT_GID`/`AT_SECURE` absent from the auxv, `__init_libc` takes an early
return that skips its `ppoll`; `__init_ssp(NULL)` derives the stack canary
arithmetically; and `__init_tls` uses its static `builtin_tls` because the
program has no `PT_TLS`. The fork's `MINIXRS.md` records each of those facts,
re-derived against v1.2.6 rather than assumed.

### `ioctl` is load-bearing

Answering `-ENOTTY` is not merely harmless. `__stdout_write` sets `f->lbf = -1`
when `TIOCGWINSZ` fails, which makes stdout **fully buffered** — so `printf`
output does not appear when it is called, but when `exit()` runs `__stdio_exit`.
A boot log containing `Hello from C!` therefore proves the flush path too, not
just formatting.

## What a `write` actually does

```
hello.c   printf(…)
musl      vfprintf → __stdio_write → __syscall(SYS_writev, …)
fork      __minixrs_syscall → VFS_WRITE (SENDREC to VFS)
VFS       issues a CPF_MAGIC grant over the caller's buffer → CDEV_WRITE
TTY       SYS_SAFECOPY pulls the bytes in, writes the PL011
```

The buffer never leaves the caller's address space until the driver copies it,
and it moves in exactly **one** copy. VFS names the grant's owner from the
kernel-stamped `m_source`, never from the payload — a caller-supplied owner
would turn VFS into a confused deputy, since VFS holds `SYS_PROC` and its
clients do not.

## Building

```sh
tools/build-musl.sh     # configure + make into target/musl-sysroot
cargo kernel-aarch64    # build.rs compiles and links userland/hello
```

The sysroot build uses `clang --target=aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` with `AR` and
`RANLIB` from the pinned Rust toolchain (`llvm-ar`, and `llvm-ar s` in place of
`llvm-ranlib`, which that toolchain does not ship). Linking uses `rust-lld` —
no platform linker and no Homebrew LLVM anywhere in the path.

`build-musl.sh` also runs the **real** errno check that slice 5.0 deferred to
here: it compiles the generated `<minixrs/errno.h>`'s opt-in POSIX block against
the fork's own `bits/errno.h`, so a POSIX errno whose magnitude drifted from
musl's is a build failure. Until this slice, CI could only prove macro
spellings.

### If the sysroot is missing

`kernel/build.rs` presence-checks `target/musl-sysroot/.stamp`. When it is
absent or stale it emits a `cargo::warning` and packs the `worker` ELF **under
the name `hello`**, so a fresh clone still boots green and only the
hello-specific markers go missing. It deliberately does not build the sysroot
itself — a multi-minute libc build launched from a cargo build script would turn
a first `cargo kernel-aarch64` into a mystery.

## `hello.ld`

The linker script starts from `userland/worker/user.ld` and keeps the parts that
are load-bearing there: page-aligned `PT_LOAD`s, no dynamic sections, a 1 MiB
load base, and the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom that puts `PT_LOAD` #0 at file offset
`0`. That idiom is **mandatory** here rather than merely nice: without it lld's
default 64 KiB page size leaves `e_phoff` in an unmapped prefix, and musl's
`__init_tls` walks the program headers from exactly the `AT_PHDR` the kernel
reports.

What it adds is everything a musl link brings that a Rust one does not, all of
it from `crti.o` / `crtn.o` / `libc.a`: `.init` and `.fini` (which define the
`_init`/`_fini` that `crt1.c` hands to `__libc_start_main`), `.init_array` /
`.fini_array` with their bracketing symbols, `.got`, and `.data.rel.ro`. Every
input section gets an explicit home, because an orphan placed past the last
`PT_LOAD` is a **silent** load failure — the kernel maps what the program
headers describe and never sees it.

Verify any change with:

```sh
"$(rustc --print sysroot)"/lib/rustlib/*/bin/llvm-readobj --program-headers \
  --elf-output-style=GNU target/hello/hello
```

## Quad-float builtins

musl's `vfprintf` references soft-float `binary128` helpers (`__multf3`,
`__floatsitf`, …): aarch64's `long double` is IEEE quad with no hardware
support. musl's `configure` finds no runtime library on this host, so those
symbols would be undefined at link time.

They come from the pinned toolchain's own `compiler_builtins`, built for the
custom `aarch64-unknown-minixrs` target by the server builds that run first.
Note that the *prebuilt* `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does
**not** export the C-ABI names — only the `-Zbuild-std` one does.

## The ELF brand

The kernel refuses to load an unbranded ELF. For Rust binaries the 28-byte
`.note.minixrs.ident` note comes from `minixrs_abi_note::brand!()`; for C it is
emitted from `crt/crt1.c` as a `.pushsection` global asm, so every C program is
branded with no opt-in. `crt1.o` is linked explicitly rather than pulled from an
archive, so — unlike a `libc.a` member — it can never be dropped by
archive-member selection.

Regressing it fails the **kernel build**, not the boot: `kernel/build.rs` runs
the same `scan_brand` check when it packs the boot archive.

## The ABI freeze

Slice 5.6 is the ABI freeze point (phase-5 decision D8). There is now C that
depends on the message layout, the call numbers, the endpoint encoding, and the
errno values, and it lives in a **different repository**. Past this slice those
change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos together.

  the last cheap moment: `src/minixrs/` and `__minixrs_syscall` in the fork, and
  on this side the generated C surface too — `include/minixrs/*.h`,
  `_MINIXRS_OFFSETOF`, `MINIXRS_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`. Prose citing *MINIX 3's*
  own headers (`callnr_h.rs`'s deviation note, `com_h.rs`'s `<minix/const.h>`)
  was deliberately left alone. The `minix-ipc/` **directory** was renamed
  `minixrs-ipc/` to match its long-standing package name.
- **`PM_EXEC` gained a 16-byte name payload** (`PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF`), replacing
  PM's hardcoded `EXEC_TARGET`, and **init alternates `worker` / `hello`**
  (`EXEC_TARGETS`) rather than flipping outright — the written scope's "flips
  `worker` → `hello`" predates 5.5 making `worker` the exec-stack probe, and
  flipping would have retired `[exec] … auxv=4` and `init: exec stack ok`.
  Groundwork 5.9's path form needs anyway. Reading the name uses a new
  host-tested `server-rt::payload::rd_name`.
- **The fallback presence-checks the SYSROOT, not the submodule**
  (`target/musl-sysroot/.stamp`). Checking the submodule would let a fresh clone
  that ran `git submodule update` but not `tools/build-musl.sh` trigger a
  multi-minute libc build from inside a cargo build script.
- **`RANLIB` is `llvm-ar s`, not `llvm-ranlib`** — the pinned toolchain ships
  `llvm-ar` but not `llvm-ranlib`.
- **Quad-float builtins had to be sourced.** musl's `vfprintf` references
  `__multf3` / `__floatsitf` / … (aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad, no
  hardware support) and musl's configure finds no runtime library on this host.
  They come from the toolchain's own `compiler_builtins` **as built by
  `-Zbuild-std` for `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`**; the prebuilt
  `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does *not* export the C-ABI

  `.init`/`.fini`, `.init_array`/`.fini_array` with bracketing symbols, `.got`,

General rule for any probe reporting through an exit status: **encode the pass, never the absence of a failure**

- **C on minix.rs — the musl port, the sysroot, and the ABI freeze (slice 5.6, milestone A):** the libc is a **git submodule at `external/musl`** → `minixrs/musl-minixrs`, tracking branch **`minixrs`** (the port; `main` is a pristine upstream mirror with nothing on it), based on tag **`v1.2.6`**. The old `KevinBarnard/musl-minix` is archived and nothing was carried over. The fork's whole delta is `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` + `src/minixrs/` + a brand block in `crt/crt1.c` + `MINIXRS.md`, and staying that small is the design goal — **musl globs `src/*/`, so `src/minixrs/` needs no Makefile edit**. Every `__syscallN` calls `__minixrs_syscall`, which switches on the *Linux* number musl still emits and issues a server round-trip (`writev`/`write` → `VFS_WRITE`, `exit`/`exit_group` → `PM_EXIT`, `set_tid_address` → 1, `ioctl` → `-ENOTTY`, everything else `-ENOSYS`); musl's ~297 call sites stay untouched, which is what lets ~1900 files rebase for free. `syscall_ret.c` is untouched because D7's magnitudes (`1..=40`, `>=200`) all sit inside its `> -4096UL` window. **`ioctl` → `-ENOTTY` is load-bearing**: it makes `__stdout_write` set `f->lbf = -1`, so stdout is **fully buffered** and `printf` only reaches the console via `exit()`'s `__stdio_exit` — the milestone marker therefore proves the flush path too. Six syscalls suffice only because of startup facts that must be **re-verified, never assumed, on any musl bump** (all re-read against v1.2.6, recorded in the fork's `MINIXRS.md`): `__init_libc` early-returns past its `ppoll` when `AT_UID`/`AT_GID`/`AT_SECURE` are absent (they read 0); `__init_ssp(NULL)` derives the canary arithmetically; `__init_tp`'s only syscall is `set_tid_address` (`__set_thread_area` is `msr tpidr_el0` inline asm since v1.2.6) and it **walks `libc.auxv`**, so the auxv must stay `AT_NULL`-terminated; `__init_tls` uses static `builtin_tls` absent a `PT_TLS` (so no `mmap`) and walks 5.5's `AT_PHDR`/`AT_PHNUM`/`AT_PHENT`. **`tools/build-musl.sh`** builds an out-of-tree sysroot into `target/musl-sysroot` (the submodule work tree stays **pristine** — the `c-headers` job asserts a clean `git status`), keyed by a `.stamp` of submodule SHA + toolchain; `RANLIB` is **`llvm-ar s`**, because the pinned toolchain ships `llvm-ar` but **not `llvm-ranlib``**. It also runs the **real D7 errno *value* check** 5.0 deferred here — the opt-in POSIX block compiled against the fork's own `bits/errno.h` under `-nostdinc -isystem <sysroot>/include`; the CI `c-headers` job keeps only the hermetic stand-in check. `userland/hello` is **not a cargo crate** — `hello.c` + `hello.ld` compiled by clang and linked by `rust-lld` inside `kernel/build.rs::build_hello`, packed under proc_nr `-1` like `worker`. **The fallback presence-checks the SYSROOT (`.stamp`), not the submodule**, and packs the `worker` ELF *under the name* `hello` with a `cargo::warning` — checking the submodule would let a fresh clone trigger a multi-minute libc build from inside a build script. musl's `vfprintf` needs soft-float **binary128** builtins (`__multf3`/`__floatsitf`/…; aarch64 `long double` is IEEE quad) which musl's configure finds no library for: they come from **`compiler_builtins` as built by `-Zbuild-std` for `aarch64-unknown-minixrs`** — the *prebuilt* `aarch64-unknown-none` rlib in the rustup sysroot does **not** export the C-ABI names, so glob the nested target dir, never the sysroot. `hello.ld` is `worker/user.ld` plus what only a musl link brings — `.init`/`.fini` (they define the `_init`/`_fini` `crt1.c` passes to `__libc_start_main`), `.init_array`/`.fini_array` with bracketing symbols, `.got`, `.data.rel.ro` — because **an orphan section past the last `PT_LOAD` is a silent load failure**; the `FILEHDR PHDRS` idiom is mandatory (not just an auxv nicety as for Rust: `__init_tls` dereferences `AT_PHDR`). No `PT_TLS` — musl keeps `errno` in the pthread struct via `tpidr_el0`, so `libc.a` has no `.tdata`/`.tbss`. **The 4 KiB exec stack was measured sufficient (~2 KB worst chain) and was NOT grown** — but v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` allocates a **VLA** (~512 B for `%f`, **~7.4 KB for `%Lf`**), so a future C program printing a `long double` will overflow it and *no static frame scan will predict that*. `PM_EXEC` gained a name payload (`PM_EXEC_NAME_OFF`, reusing `EXEC_NAME_LEN`), PM's `EXEC_TARGET` is gone, and **init alternates `worker`/`hello`** (`EXEC_TARGETS`, worker **first** — `probe_pid` keys 5.5's verdict on the first child) so the exec-stack proof survives the C milestone; the target is chosen *before* the fork so both halves of the SENDREC agree. The boot marker is **`name=hello entry=` with no `target=` slot**: init's fork pool gives `hello` slot 15 stub-free but **16** with stubs, so a slot-keyed marker passes in one config and is vacuous in the other. **ABI freeze (D8): past this slice `Message` layout, call numbers, endpoints, and errnos change only via a deliberate ABI-bump PR touching both repos** — there is now C in another repository depending on all four. input.new_string:
/*
	 * The milestone.
	 *
	 * This particular line goes out IMMEDIATELY, and the reason is worth
	 * knowing: musl's stdout starts *line* buffered (`.lbf = '\n'`), and it is
	 * __stdout_write -- called for the first flush -- that sets `f->lbf = -1`
	 * after the fork's ioctl answers -ENOTTY. So this write trips the
	 * line-buffered path on the way through, and every printf AFTER it is
	 * fully buffered and reaches the console only when exit() runs
	 * __stdio_exit. The `errno ok` and `iov ok` lines below are the ones that
	 * prove the flush path.
	 */
	printf("minix.rs hello: Hello from C!\n");

	/* stderr is unbuffered, so this one goes out immediately too -- a
	 * different descriptor and a different buffering mode through the same VFS
	 * path. */
	fprintf(stderr, "minix.rs hello: stderr works\n");

	/*
	 * The two-iovec path -- the only thing in this program that makes the
	 * fork's iovec loop matter, and it has to be set up deliberately.
	 *
	 * __stdio_write hands writev iovs[0] = whatever is PENDING in the stream
	 * buffer and iovs[1] = the new data. Both are non-empty only when a write
	 * too big for the remaining buffer arrives while bytes are still pending.
	 * So: leave a short line pending (stdout is fully buffered by now, so it
	 * stays), then write a block that cannot fit beside it.
	 *
	 * Get this wrong -- write the big block while the buffer is empty -- and
	 * iovs[0] is skipped, the call carries ONE iovec, and a writev that
	 * ignores every iovec after the first passes anyway.
	 *
	 * Two independent halves of the proof, the slice-5.4 shape: the `iov-end`
	 * tail only reaches the console if the SECOND iovec was sent, and
	 * `match=1` says fwrite accounted for every byte. Neither subsumes the
	 * other.
	 */
	printf("minix.rs hello: iov ");
	memset(big, '.', sizeof big);
	memcpy(big + sizeof big - 8, "iov-end\n", 8);
	wrote = fwrite(big, 1, sizeof big, stdout);
	printf("minix.rs hello: iov %s\n",
	       wrote == sizeof big ? "ok match=1" : "FAIL");

* The FILEHDR PHDRS idiom on the text segment is MANDATORY, not cosmetic.
 * Without it lld's default aarch64 max-page-size (64 KiB) puts PT_LOAD #0 at

input.new_string:
* The FILEHDR PHDRS idiom on the text segment is what gives this binary an
 * AT_PHDR. Without it lld's default aarch64 max-page-size (64 KiB) puts
 * PT_LOAD #0 at file offset 0x10000, leaving `e_phoff` in an unmapped prefix,
 * so SYS_EXEC has no mapped VA to report.
 *
 * Measured consequence today (slice 5.6, mutation-tested): the auxv drops from
 * 4 entries to 1 and hello still runs. That is not luck — `do_exec` OMITS
 * AT_PHDR rather than reporting an unmapped one, and musl's `__init_tls` then
 * walks zero program headers, finds no PT_TLS, and falls back to its static
 * `builtin_tls`, which is what this program uses anyway.
 *
 * Keep the idiom regardless. It is the difference between "there is no TLS
 * image" and "we could not look", and those stop being the same answer the
 * moment libc or this program gains a PT_TLS — at which point the failure is
 * silently wrong thread-local storage rather than a link error.

Implementation and verification are complete. The only thing left needs commits, which your auto-mode rule says to surface first.

**Verified end-to-end** — milestone A is real:
```
minix.rs hello: Hello from C!      ← printf → VFS → TTY, from C
minix.rs hello: errno ok           ← D7 errno identity, at runtime
minix.rs hello: iov ok match=1     ← two-iovec writev
```
63/63 boot markers pass in the default config; all 5.5 markers survive alongside the new ones; stub-free config clean; fmt, both kernel clippy gates, workspace clippy, and 8 test suites green.

**Five findings worth flagging** — four are places the plan's expectations didn't survive contact:

1. **The errno check was vacuous when first written.** macOS `sed` has no `\b`, so `CHECK_MACRO` kept the old spelling while CI/script defined the new one — the guarded block compiled **0** assertions. Now 40, and mutation-proven (`libc EDEADLK disagrees with kernel-shared error.rs`).
2. **The plan's `target=15 name=hello` marker would have failed CI.** `hello` is slot **16** with stubs, 15 only stub-free. Keyed on `name=hello entry=` instead.
3. **Mutation 2 initially proved nothing.** `hello` never produced two non-empty iovecs (musl's stdout starts *line*-buffered, so the first `printf` flushes and leaves the buffer empty). I restructured `hello.c` to set the case up deliberately; the mutation now hangs the program and drops all four markers.
4. **`llvm-ranlib` doesn't ship** with the pinned toolchain (`llvm-ar s` instead), and musl needed **quad-float builtins** — sourced from the `-Zbuild-std` `compiler_builtins`, since the prebuilt sysroot rlib doesn't export the C-ABI names. No LLVM build added.
5. **The 4 KiB exec stack was sufficient** (~2 KB measured) — §7's growth wasn't needed. But v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` uses a **VLA**: ~7.4 KB for `%Lf`. A future C program printing a `long double` will overflow it, and no static scan predicts it. Recorded in CLAUDE.md and the plan.

I also did the `minix-ipc/` → `minixrs-ipc/` rename you asked for (53 files, workspace green).

| Path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `arch/aarch64/syscall_arch.h` | `__syscall0..6` call `__minixrs_syscall`; VDSO macros deleted |
| `src/thread/aarch64/syscall_cp.s` | `__syscall_cp_asm` forwards to the port instead of `svc` |
| `src/minixrs/ipc.c` | The `svc #0` IPC trap |
| `src/minixrs/_syscall.c` | Linux syscall number → server IPC |
| `src/minixrs/minixrs_internal.h` | Shared declarations for the two above |
| `crt/crt1.c` | The 28-byte `.note.minixrs.ident` ELF brand |
| `MINIXRS.md` | This file |

Nothing else. `git diff v1.2.6 --stat` should show exactly three modified files
outside `src/minixrs/`.

### Why `syscall_cp.s` is in the delta

It is not enough to redirect `syscall_arch.h`. Cancellable syscalls — `read`,
`write`, `open`, `close`, … — go through `__syscall_cp`, and **which
implementation that resolves to is decided by linkage**:

- `src/thread/__syscall_cp.c` supplies a **weak** `__syscall_cp_c` that calls
  `__syscall`, and therefore the port.
- `src/thread/pthread_cancel.c` supplies a **strong** one that calls
  `__syscall_cp_asm`, which upstream ends with a bare `svc 0`.

A program that never touches `pthread_cancel` gets the safe path by accident. A
program that does silently routes every cancellable syscall onto a raw Linux
trap — which on minix.rs means the kernel reads x0/x1/x2 as an endpoint, a
primitive, and a message pointer. So `__syscall_cp_asm` forwards to
`__minixrs_syscall` instead, and the behaviour no longer depends on what else
got linked.

Cancellation itself is a no-op (no threads yet); the `__cp_begin`/`__cp_end`/
`__cp_cancel` labels are preserved so the file's shape survives until a slice
adds threads.

### Linux traps that deliberately remain

Three assembly files still contain a raw Linux `svc`, and none is reachable
today. Porting them would mean inventing a threading and signal-delivery model
minix.rs does not have yet, so they are recorded rather than rewritten:

| File | Symbol | Becomes reachable when |
|---|---|---|
| `src/signal/aarch64/restore.s` | `__restore_rt` | signal handlers are delivered to user space |
| `src/thread/aarch64/clone.s` | `__clone` | threads exist |
| `src/thread/aarch64/__unmapself.s` | `__unmapself` | threads exist (teardown) |

Audit any linked binary with:

```sh
llvm-objdump -d <binary> | awk '/^[0-9a-f]+ </{fn=$2} /\tsvc\t/{print fn, $0}'
```

A single-threaded C program must show exactly **one** hit, in `__minixrs_ipc`.

```

It emits `include/minix/{ipc,com,callnr,errno}.h`, plus two artifacts that make
the CI gate real: `abi-selftest.c` — a header is never a translation unit on its
own, so without a `.c` file none of the generated `_Static_assert`s would ever
fire — and `abi-check/errno.h`, a CI-only stand-in for the C library's
`<errno.h>`.

Two things the headers are careful about:

- **`_PROC_NR` vs `_EP`.** Every process gets both. minix.rs sign-extends the
  endpoint proc field instead of using MINIX 3's offset bias, so for the kernel
  tasks the boot endpoint is *not* the process number (`SYSTEM_PROC_NR` is −2,
  `SYSTEM_EP` is 32766). Naming a task by its `_PROC_NR` in an IPC call is a bug,
  and the header asserts the C decode macro against the Rust-computed endpoints.
- **The POSIX errno block is asserted, never defined.** minix.rs adopts musl's
  numbering verbatim, so those values must come from the C library's own
  `<errno.h>`; `minix/errno.h` defines only the MINIX 200-band and puts the
  POSIX checks behind `MINIX_ABI_CHECK_POSIX_ERRNO`, which the musl build
  defines. See [System Calls & ABI](reference/syscalls.md).

## Debugging: QEMU trace forensics

User-space servers run at EL0 with no console — they cannot print. All server
behavior is observed through kernel-side traces (`[as]`, `[ipc]`, `[ksys]`,
`[pf]`, `[alarm]`). Reading those logs has some sharp edges worth knowing:

input.new_string:
init is a plain `minixrs-ipc` program — no SEF, because it is not a server. The rest
of its body is a respawn loop: `PM_FORK`; the child (`m_type == 0`) issues
`PM_EXEC` naming the binary it wants to become; the parent (`m_type > 0`) issues
`PM_WAIT` to reap the zombie, then loops. Each cycle recycles a fork-pool slot
with a fresh endpoint generation — observable in the boot trace as repeating
`SYS_FORK` → `SYS_EXEC` → `SYS_EXIT` triples, the proof that fork, exec,
teardown, and reap all compose.

Since slice 5.6 the exec target is the *caller's* choice — `PM_EXEC` carries a
name, rather than PM hardcoding one — and init **alternates** between two
binaries, so the trace shows `name=worker` and `name=hello` on successive
cycles:

- **`worker`** is slice 5.5's exec-ABI probe. It validates the SysV initial
  stack against its own `sp` and reports the verdict as its exit status, which
  init prints once (keyed on the child's *pid*, because PM parents the demo
  stubs to init and stub D's deliberate SIGSEGV would otherwise be the first
  thing reaped).
- **`hello`** is slice 5.6's C milestone, linked against the musl fork.

Alternating rather than switching is deliberate: retiring `worker` to make room
for `hello` would have taken the exec-ABI proof down with it. See
[C Library & musl Port](../libc/overview.md).

input.old_string:
MUSL_SHA=$(git -C "$MUSL_SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
TOOLCHAIN_ID=$(
	{ cat "$ROOT/rust-toolchain.toml" 2>/dev/null || true; clang --version | head -1; } \

input.new_string:
MUSL_SHA=$(git -C "$MUSL_SRC" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)

# Hash portably. macOS ships `shasum` (perl) but no `sha256sum`; Linux ships
# `sha256sum` (coreutils) and usually but not always `shasum`. `cksum` is in
# POSIX and is the last resort -- it is a weak checksum, but this only has to
# detect a toolchain CHANGE, not resist an adversary.
#
# Failing loudly matters: a hash command that printed nothing would make every
# stamp compare equal, and the sysroot would silently never rebuild.
hash_stdin() {
	if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		sha256sum
	elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		shasum -a 256
	elif command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
		openssl dgst -sha256 | sed 's/.*= //'
	else
		cksum
	fi
}

TOOLCHAIN_ID=$(
	{ cat "$ROOT/rust-toolchain.toml" 2>/dev/null || true; clang --version | head -1; } \
		| hash_stdin | cut -d' ' -f1
)
if [ -z "$TOOLCHAIN_ID" ]; then
	echo "error: could not hash the toolchain identity (no sha256sum/shasum/openssl/cksum?)" >&2
	exit 1
fi
WANT="musl=$MUSL_SHA toolchain=$TOOLCHAIN_ID"

Both PRs are open and CI is running; I'll report as checks land.

**Delivered — Phase 5 milestone A:**
- **[minixrs/musl-minixrs#1](https://github.com/minixrs/musl-minixrs/pull/1)** — the port (7 files, based on upstream v1.2.6)
- **[minixrs/minixrs#47](https://github.com/minixrs/minixrs/pull/47)** — the minix.rs side (61 files)

Neither is merged. The fork's `minixrs` branch is the PR base; merging #1 with a regular merge preserves `f1db256f`, which is what #47's submodule pins.

**Two defects that only surfaced by running things, not reading them:**

1. **The D7 errno check was vacuous when I first wrote it.** macOS `sed` has no `\b`, so `CHECK_MACRO` kept its old spelling while CI and the script defined the new one — the guarded block compiled **zero** assertions and reported success. Now 40, mutation-proven against musl's real `bits/errno.h`.
2. **The worker-as-hello fallback tripped a *forbidden* marker.** `worker` validates `argv[0]` against the exact bytes the kernel wrote and hardcoded `b"worker"`, so a missing sysroot printed `worker: stack FAIL` — an absent optional dependency looking identical to a broken exec ABI. Both Grok reviews and my own reading passed over the name-level substitution; only booting that config caught it. `ARGV0_NAMES` is now `{worker, hello}`.

**Deviations from the plan worth your attention:**
- The plan's marker `target=15 name=hello` would have **failed CI** — `hello` is slot 16 with stubs. Keyed on `name=hello entry=` instead.
- The 4 KiB exec stack was measured sufficient (~2 KB) and **not** grown. But v1.2.6's `fmt_fp` is a VLA: ~7.4 KB for `%Lf`. The next C program that prints a `long double` will overflow it, and no static scan predicts that — recorded in CLAUDE.md and the plan.
- `llvm-ranlib` doesn't ship with the toolchain (`llvm-ar s`), and quad-float builtins had to come from the `-Zbuild-std` `compiler_builtins` rather than the prebuilt rlib.

**One item I did not touch:** the tooling repo (`~/src/tooling`) has stale references your cross-repo rule says belong in a separate session — `scripts/export-patches.sh:14,49` still default `MINIXRS_MUSL_BASE` to `v1.2.5`, and `docs/roadmap.md:27,59` still say phase 5 is at slice 5.3 with P3 blocked on 5.4/5.5/5.6.
